title: Test vectors for draft-dias-agent-payment-verdicts-00
warning: TEST ONLY. Every signature in these vectors is made with, or derived from, the keys in testKeys, which include the example key of Appendix A of the draft and are published so that anyone can reproduce and extend the vectors. The issuers are the reserved example domains https://issuer.example and https://issuer-b.example. Nothing signed with them proves anything. Never configure these keys or key sets in a verifier that protects real payments.

conventions.issuers: Map from each accepted issuer identifier to the name of its key set in keySets. A kid that is absent from the set stays absent after the one refetch of step 4.
conventions.mode: "settle": Section 6, all twelve steps. "record": Section 6.2, checking a stored verdict.
conventions.payment: Settle mode: the relying party's payment record after any conversion of Section 4.3: amount in the agreed unit (major units), as a decimal string; currency code in the form the issuer uses.
conventions.agreedMandates: Settle mode: mandate identifiers the operator has agreed with the relying party (step 8), for every issuer in issuers. Every settle-mode vector is a payment that draws on that operator's funds, so the mandate check of step 8 always applies.
conventions.seenNonces: Settle mode: pairs [iss, nonce] of verdicts already accepted (step 12).
conventions.seenJtis: Settle mode: pairs [iss, jti] of the same accepted verdicts, for a verifier that records jti instead of nonce (step 12). Use whichever your verifier records.
conventions.seenSupersedes: Settle mode: pairs [iss, supersedes] already accepted (Section 10.12).
conventions.testingOnly: Settle mode: whether the verifier is used only for testing (step 3).
conventions.receivedAt: Record mode: when the verdict was received, Unix seconds, or null if not recorded.
conventions.distinguishTest: Record mode: whether the checking party applies step 3.
conventions.refetchWouldReturn: Record mode, where present: the key set a refetch from the issuer would return now. A record checker MUST NOT refetch (Section 6.2); the field lets a test detect one that does.
conventions.audience: The verifier's own identifier for the aud rule of step 6, or null.
conventions.nestingDepth: Every vector assumes a JSON nesting-depth bound (step 1) of at least 4.
conventions.expected: The expected results assume that every SHOULD-level rejection of Section 6 and Section 10.12 is applied; notes name the vectors that depend on one. valid MUST match. step is the first step of Section 6, in the document's order, that rejects the token; a verifier that runs the steps in another order, as Section 6 permits, can report a different step. note gives known alternatives.

vectors.description: The token of Appendix A.2, checked as Appendix A.3 describes.
The Appendix A token with S replaced by n - S. Both signatures are valid (step 5 forbids requiring low S); the claims, and so the nonce, are the same.
request.amount 12.5 against a payment record of 12.50: equal by decimal value (step 9).
request.amount 0.5 against 0.500000.

request.amount 999999999999999.999999, the largest amount the issuer writes, against the same amount. Equal by decimal value. The amount is above 2^30, so a binary64 comparison is not permitted; a verifier that reads the claim as binary64 (1000000000000000) and compares that with the record's decimal value rejects this valid verdict.
An allow from an operator's approval of a review: supersedes names the review verdict.
An allow with a private claim and a member of request that this document does not define; verifiers ignore both (Section 4.2).
Signed with the test key sandbox-example-1, checked by a verifier used only for testing (step 3).
Checked at exp + 59 s: inside the 60-second allowance (step 7).
iat is 60 s after the verifier's clock: at the limit of the allowance (step 7).
nbf is 60 s after the verifier's clock: not rejected (step 7).
aud is an array that contains the verifier's identifier (step 6).
aud is a string equal to the verifier's identifier (step 6).
A non-ASCII recipient that matches the payment record code point for code point.
A verifier that accepts two issuers; the token comes from the second, with that issuer's key.
The nonce store holds the same nonce for another issuer; the replay key is the pair of iss and nonce (step 12).
The payload segment keeps its base64 padding (=), and the signature covers the padded segment. Many base64 decoders accept padding; step 1 rejects it.
A line break inside the payload segment, covered by the signature.
The payload segment uses '+' or '/' from the standard base64 alphabet instead of '-' and '_', and the signature covers it as written.
A header segment whose length is 1 modulo 4, covered by the signature. No base64 encoding has that length; some decoders drop the extra character.
Only header and payload, no signature segment.
Five segments, shaped like a JWE, with a readable payload in the ciphertext position.

The payload contains a byte that is not valid UTF-8 inside the recipient; the signature covers it. The payment record's recipient ends in U+FFFD, so a decoder that substitutes U+FFFD instead of rejecting accepts it.
The payload is a JSON array holding the claims object, not an object.
The payload has iss twice: the configured issuer first, then another.

expected.note: A verifier whose parser keeps the lexically last member rejects it at step 4 instead.

vectors.description: request has recipient twice: the payment's payee first, then another.

expected.note: Rests on step 1's SHOULD to reject duplicates at any depth (a MUST for a verifier that parses the payload more than once). A parser that keeps the last member rejects it at step 11; one that keeps the first member and does not apply the SHOULD accepts it.

vectors.description: The header has kid twice: example-1 first, then sandbox-example-1, whose key signed the token.

expected.note: A parser that keeps the last member rejects it at step 3; one that keeps the first, which step 1 forbids, rejects it at step 5.
